text:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — spotted an inconsistent example in the API ref for POST /v1/generate. The docs show the optional query param `include_metadata` as a string (e.g. `?include_metadata=\"true\"`) in the cURL example, but runtime expects a boolean query flag or omission. This breaks the fetch-based SDK snippet (returns 400 in edge cases).

Marta López: ugh, thanks for catching. Where's the example? can you paste the snippet?

Alex Chen: Sure — current problematic curl:
```
curl -X POST 
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?include_metadata="true"' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-large","prompt":"hi"}'
```
Behavior: servers parse querystrings literally so quotes make it a string; should be `?include_metadata=true` or moved into JSON body as `include_metadata: true` per API conventions.

Rick Patel: Good catch. I can open a quick docs PR to update the curl + JS snippet. Also need to check the Ruby and Go examples (they use SDKs that currently set this flag via params object, which is fine).

Maya Singh: Also note: we have a migration note for older clients that used the querystring-only approach. Might be worth adding a short note in the ref: "Prefer body param for booleans; if using query flags, do not quote the value."

Alex Chen: Agreed. Proposed edits:
- Fix curl example to `?include_metadata=true`
- Update fetch/Node snippet to pass include_metadata as boolean in the JSON body
- Add a one-line migration note under the param: "legacy clients sometimes sent stringified booleans; ensure unquoted boolean values or use body param"

Marta López: that sounds right. Rick — can you include the migration note in the same PR? Tag me for copy edits.

Rick Patel: Yep. I'll draft PR now. Quick question: do we need to change any server-side fallback to accept quoted booleans? feels risky.

Maya Singh: Not ideal — accepting both creates sloppy contract; prefer docs fix only and add a short deprecation note for quoted strings so integrators have time to update.

Alex Chen: For the JS snippet, use this pattern:
```js
// Node fetch example: include_metadata in body as boolean
await fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-large', prompt: 'hi', include_metadata: true })
})
```

Marta López: Nice. Also add a short test step for the docs CI: run the cURL example in a dry-run mode to ensure it returns 200/created sample. I'll add a checklist item in the PR template.

docs-bot: PR created by rick-patel: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1287 — title: "docs(generate): fix include_metadata example, add migration note"

Rick Patel: PR up, PTAL @Marta López @Maya Singh. I updated curl, JS, Ruby snippet comment, and added migration note under the param docs. Also added a one-line changelog.

Marta López: Reviewing now. Small nit: change wording from "legacy clients" to "older clients" and put the example quoted string in monospace.

Maya Singh: LGTM from API behavior side. I verified that no server change is required.

Alex Chen: Thanks — looks good. Can we also add a short callout in the Generate endpoint overview: "Boolean query flags must be unquoted" so it's easy to spot?

Rick Patel: Added that line. Tests: I ran the curl example locally against staging and got a 200. Updated the docs CI sample test to use `--silent --fail` so it fails if status != 2xx.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for staging: docs-site/docs@staging build #8421

Marta López: Merged and deployed to staging. I'll schedule a quick smoke test and then merge to main after copy check.

Alex Chen: Awesome — thanks everyone. Filing a micro task to follow up on telemetry to catch quoted booleans in requests (so we can surface common integrator errors).

Rick Patel: Filed as ENG-1123. Closing thread after main merge. :tada:
